•

• 
 
It is known for its rhythmic footwork, intricate gestures, fast spins, and expressive storytelling.

 
 
•

•

•

It is known for its grace, fluidity, and devotion to the theme of Radha and Krishna, the divine lovers from Hindu mythology.

 
 
•

• It is a form of **Tamil folk dance** and is popular in **South India**, especially Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance involves carrying** Kavadi, a semi-circular decorated canopy, **on the shoulders while dancing to the beats of** traditional drums and music. **
 
• The devotees performing Kavadi attam often **pierce their skin** with small hooks or skewers as an act of** penance and devotion.**

__

• And sway with the soles of their feet perched on the top of a glass and also sometimes on the edge of a naked sword.
 
• This dance is believed to be originated in Gujarat.
 
• And was soon picked up and adopted by the local tribal men and women of Rajasthan.
